maria: Quick follow-up to the slice/streaming RFC — I'm thinking about a lightweight way for the edge to publish 'cut points' so clients (and the gateway) can resume or charge incrementally if a connection drops. idea: append a tiny trailer with an opaque resume token + byte/token index every N tokens. Could be used for: billing checkpoints, cheaper partial retries, and client-side resume of long-generations. Thoughts?

aj: Interesting. Main pain is proxies that don't preserve trailers (esp older HTTP/1.1 paths). With HTTP/2/3 it's doable, but we need explicit guarantees: trailers must be proxied end-to-end. Also need to consider QUIC coalescing behavior — trailers may get delayed which hurts perceived EOF.

chloe: Two quick cautions: 1) resume tokens + partial replays + side effects => hard correctness problem. If a generation triggers a tool call or DB write, resuming can cause duplication. 2) accounting: we must ensure checkpoints are deterministic token boundaries (or we double-bill). Opaque token is fine but calibrate at model/runtime boundary.

sam: +1 to preserving only for idempotent/read-only streams. For tool-calls we should reject resume or force full replay with strong idempotency keys. Proposal: negotiate capability via a header on request start `X-Stream-Resume: accept` and runtime will only emit trailers when both edge and model instance agree. Example handshake: 
```
client -> edge: POST /v1/generate 
  X-Stream-Resume: accept
edge -> backend: X-Stream-Resume: accept
backend -> edge (trailers): resume-token: RTk_abc123; token-pos: 4096
```
This keeps the edge from inventing tokens.

leo: Also watch latency: streaming trailers require a flush/finish. If we emit a trailer every N tokens, that implies frequent flushes which can kill throughput. Maybe use coarse checkpoints (every 2-5s or 4k tokens). For HTTP/2 paths, trailers are cheap, but for HTTP/1.1 or legacy frontdoors we'll fall back to in-body JSON checkpoints (more verbose).

maria: Nice tradeoffs. Action items: 1) small PoC that emits `resume-token` trailer from runtime for text-gen (no tool calls) with 4k-token windows, 2) EDGE: add `X-Stream-Resume` passthrough and opt-in feature flag, 3) Eval: test resume correctness across gRPC/h2/h1 fallbacks and measure tail latency when checkpoints emitted. I'll spin up a test harness. tagging: @aj @chloe for infra/consistency checks, @sam for billing semantics. :thumbsup:
